title.narrative: Continued cooperation between SwEPA and KEPA 2025-2027
Continued cooperation between SwEPA and KEPA 2025-2027

description.narrative:
The project is a continuation of the previous cooperation between the Kosovo Environmental Protection Agency, KEPA and the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, SwEPA - which aims to pave the way for Kosovo to meet the environmental requirements to become a member of the EU. The title of the project is "Continued Cooperation between Swedish Environmental and Protection Agency - Capacity Building on Nature Protection and Environmental Data Use". The overall outcome of the project is "KEPA delivers its tasks regarding nature protection and environmental data in a more systematic, efficient and transparent way". Sida has shortened the new contribution's title to: Continued cooperation between SwEPA and KEPA 2025-2027.
Priority areas for the project are to improve data and measures when it comes to, for example, air quality, strengthened protection of national parks including biodiversity and preparation for KEPA to implement and monitor Natura 2000 areas. A red thread in the project is to build capacity for KEPA in order for the institution to strengthen its coordinating role in Kosovo for environmental data. The authority shall also lead planning and monitoring, and contribute to measures to improve the protection of Kosovo's national parks and Natura 2000 sites. Within the project, communication activities are integrated, not least to cooperate better with other actors and to reach out to the citizens. Data will be a core issue for KEPA; to improve, report and disseminate facts about the environment, which is needed for increased knowledge about the country's environmental situation and for decisions to take action.
Sida assesses that the project is well planned and has a results framework that matches the requirements for EU-accession, especially the EU Directive, Article 27, but also the EU Directive on Publicity (INSPIRE) and the EU's Habitat and Birds Directive and the Aarhus Convention. The project's priority areas are also in line with the recently approved national strategy: Kosovo Strategy for Environmental Protection 2024-2033. It is also in line with the Strategy for Sweden's Reform Cooperation with the Western Balkans and Turkey, 2021 to 2027.
At the global level, the project will contribute to Agenda 2030, as the project is in line with SDG 13, Climate Action, SDG 15 Life on Land and Goal 16, Peace, justice and strong institutions.

Detta projekt är en fortsättning på ett samarbete mellan Sveriges och Kosovos Naturvårdsverk. Baserat på deras tidigare fyra år (2020-2024) av samarbete kommer fokus för den fortsatta perioden att vara: 1) Att bygga en effektiv insamling, hantering och användning av miljödata. 2) Stärka planering, förvaltning och övervakning av skyddade områden i Kosovo. 3) Strukturera utvecklingen av Natura 2000-områden. Aktiviteterna är i linje med EU-direktiven och kommer att stödja Kosovo att bli en EU-medlem

This project is a continuation of a collaboration between Sweden's and Kosovo's agencies for Environmental and Protection. Based on their earlier four years (2020-2024) of collaboration the focus for the continued period will be: 1) Building an efficient collection, management and use of environmental data. 2) Strengthening the planning, management and monitoring of protected areas in Kosovo. 3) Structuring the development of Natura 2000 areas. The activities are in line with the EU-directives and will support Kosovo to become an EU-member.

Since the new phase of collaboration between SwEPA and KEPA started in early February, the results are yet not seen. However planning and activities have taken place.
A meeting on June 16 this year with the former long-term adviser, and previous meeting with the project leader at SwEPA plus a dialogue with the head of KEPA are the basis for this summery. The new program manager, Mr Mulla, joined the meeting.
Complementary to the points below; the Conclusion memo from last phase and the CoP written in January 2025, could be of interest, as this phase is a continuation from the previous four year period.
The following is worth mention:
- The kick-off on February 21, 2025, was according to SwEPA productive, with lots of engaged team members. There is an ambition from KEPA, to clarify the roles of the different experts better than from the last phase so that the DG doesn't take to much responsibility on a practical level.
- Two persons will be involved and responsible for each component, and from the Swedish side there will be focal points for all three goals.
- During the kick-off the different components and activities were discussed (see the goals above) and the engagement, according to the former long term adviser, was good but a bit more of engagement could be needed. For instance, there was no representation from Bjeshkët e Nemuna National Park.
- The planning has been shared with other donors, as Switzerland and Japan, so that there will be no duplication in activities.
- Regarding the cooperation with Save the Children and Utalaya Foundation the book that was launched (Uta in Sharr Mountains) and it will be used in a strategic way and probably animated. Responsibility for the coordination lies on Save the Children Kosovo. A summer School has also started, and will be part of the further planning. See below regarding following up.
- SwEPA is in contact with EU-office regarding a potential cooperation and additional action linked to the project. EU is planning - or already finished the planning - of a project that can add up to what SwEPA KEPA is doing.
- The engagement from the head of KEPA, is strong and important for the drive of the project. However, the discussion on how the team over all can take more responsibility is on-going.
- The communication will be integrated in the activities - a possible procurement will be done for the more promoting activities. However, the knowledge internally at KEPA needs to be strengthened.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
